title: Improve documentation planning and HTML output

fields.outcome: Documentation authors can agree the output structure and produce readable, branded HTML from one specification.
fields.scope: Cover planning questions for documentation output (image zoom, collapsible chapters, language approach, table-of-contents depth and parts, branding, navigation, intro or marketing content and motion-ad routing, and test accounts/roles), plus HTML rendering improvements: render Markdown text, declare document language, make single-file mode self-contained, nest and group the table of contents, link chapter references, support themes, and embed approved external content. Treat the supplied consumer feedback as draft requirements; exact schema shapes and defaults remain open.
fields.acceptance: A documentation author can capture the listed planning choices. Generated HTML renders Markdown prose and tables safely, uses the declared language, and offers nested/part-grouped navigation with links to sections. Single-file mode has no external image assets. Chapter references resolve to anchors. Themes and embeds are configurable and constrained to safe, documented inputs.
fields.verification: Add focused schema and generator coverage for Markdown rendering, language metadata, nested/grouped navigation, cross-reference links, self-contained image output, theme output, and embed validation. Review generated HTML for escaping and safe URL behavior.
fields.risks: Markdown and embed support can introduce HTML/script injection or unsafe external resource embedding. Define a restricted Markdown renderer, URL policy, iframe permissions, and theme surface during design.
fields.source: Consumer feedback supplied by the user on 2026-11-03; scope and acceptance remain discovery-stage proposals.

criteria.expectation: The planning workflow asks about image zoom, collapsible chapters, languages, table-of-contents depth and parts, branding, navigation, intro or motion content, and module roles/test accounts.
Text blocks render supported Markdown formatting, lists, tables, and notes as HTML while escaping unsafe input.
The specification declares a valid language and generated HTML uses it for the document language attribute.
Single-file HTML output embeds referenced images and does not require an assets directory.
The table of contents follows section hierarchy and supports named groups or parts.
Supported chapter references in prose become links to the referenced section.
A specification can select a documented theme or branding tokens that are applied to generated HTML.
A validated embed block can include approved external content with explicit safe frame attributes.
